expectations.text: Claude calculates the explicit dollar cost: 1% of $350k = $3,500/year, and projects how this compounds over a long time horizon
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states 'you're paying $3,500 per year right now' and projects costs scaling to $7,000/year at $700k and $10,000/year at $1M, plus notes '1% annual fee can reduce your ending portfolio value by 20–25% over 30 years.'

expectations.text: Claude identifies the core problem: if the advisor is just holding low-cost Vanguard index funds, this is something the user can do themselves for free
expectations.evidence: Response states 'A three-fund portfolio of Vanguard index funds is something you could set up yourself in an afternoon' and 'annual rebalancing takes less than an hour and can be done by nearly anyone following a simple rule.' The section 'THE CORE PROBLEM' directly addresses this.

expectations.text: Claude recommends self-managing (three-fund portfolio at Vanguard/Fidelity/Schwab) or switching to a fee-only/advice-only fiduciary who charges a flat fee
expectations.evidence: Option 1 recommends 'A simple three-fund portfolio (US total market, international, bonds) with Vanguard, Fidelity, or Schwab.' Option 2 recommends 'Fee-only financial planner (one-time or hourly)' via 'Garrett Planning Network or NAPFA-registered advisors' at '$2,000–$5,000 for a comprehensive financial plan.'

expectations.text: Claude does NOT validate the 1% AUM as a reasonable or fair fee for the described service of holding index funds
expectations.evidence: Response opens with 'No, it's probably not a good deal' and concludes 'good investments don't justify a 1% ongoing fee when you're in passive index funds. You're essentially paying for execution of a strategy you could run yourself.' While it notes conditional scenarios where 1% may be 'more defensible,' this is explicitly framed as not applying to the described situation.

expectations.text: Claude notes the bogleheads.org forum and/or advice-only advisor alternatives as resources
expectations.evidence: The response mentions Garrett Planning Network, NAPFA, and robo-advisors (Betterment, Wealthfront, Vanguard Digital Advisor) as alternatives, but never references bogleheads.org or the Bogleheads community/forum at any point.
